definition: A text generation strategy that selects the single most probable next token at each step, without considering alternative sequences.
details: Greedy decoding is fast and deterministic but can lead to suboptimal overall sequences and repetitive text, since it never reconsiders earlier choices.
story: Imagine a sketch artist who starts with static and, stroke by stroke, sharpens it into a face. The result feels creative because it is memory, reshuffled at speed. Given a starting line, the machine imagines what comes next — a word, a note, a patch of a picture. The model dreams a little, then cleans up the dream. And that is Greedy Decoding — making something new out of everything it has ever seen.
